entities.summary: Tiberius Pollienus Armenius Peregrinus was a Roman senator who played a crucial role in shaping the Roman Empire's governance and foreign policy during the 3rd century CE. Born into a family of Armenian descent, Peregrinus rose through the ranks of Roman politics, becoming consul in AD 244 and serving as a key advisor to the emperor Gordian I. His diplomatic efforts helped secure a peace treaty with the Parthian Empire, a significant achievement that showcased the Roman Empire's military and economic prowess. Peregrinus' legacy extends beyond his political accomplishments, as he also served as a patron to the Roman poet and historian, Claudian. His influence can be seen in the works of later Roman historians, who often cited him as a model of statesmanship. Peregrinus' story serves as a testament to the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the Roman Empire's rise to dominance. As the empire continued to expand, Peregrinus' diplomatic skills and strategic thinking would prove invaluable in navigating the treacherous waters of international relations. His impact on Roman history would be felt for centuries to come, as he left behind a lasting legacy of statesmanship and diplomacy.
